chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

«The divorce of the young child is nothing.» This does not contradict what we have previously mentioned, because we interpret this report as applying to one who does not possess intellect and does not know how to divorce properly, since that is considered in the occurrence of the divorce, and that which indicates this is what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is the divorce of a young child valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that a young child's divorce is not null but rather conditional upon their level of intellect (*aql*) and proficiency in the act. This ruling is reconciled with other texts by limiting the scope to those lacking full legal capacity, emphasizing that validity depends on the maturity of understanding rather than mere age. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that *talaq* requires both the capacity to understand and the intent to effect the divorce.
